title: SSD with Btrfs overheats after a first write of any kind
body: Hello, recently, my laptop SSD started to overheat significantly. I have 4 partitions, two of which are Btrfs subvolumes. The issue persists both on recent kernels (tested NixOS kernels only, 6.12.35) and also on older kernels (Arch Live ISO, 6.10.2). The following commands were run in the Live Arch tty environment. Before, the SSD temperature was about 50-60 °C, which is still high, but manageable, not it is in the range of 70-80 °C when the drive already limits the IO operations. Once I boot the Live env, the temps of the SSD are ~40 °C (obtained by smartctl). Then I run the following sequence of commands with the following results (umount skipped) mount -o ro /dev/nvme0n1p2 /mnt/root # temps are fine ls /mnt/root/@/nix/store # temps are fine mount -o noatime /dev/nvme0n1p2 /mnt/root # temps are fine ls /mnt/root/@/nix/store # temps are fine mount /dev/nvme0n1p2 /mnt/root # temps are fine # if I run either of these: ls /mnt/root/@/nix/store # temps start to rise quickly over 70 °C touch /mnt/root/@/burn.txt # same as above The rise in temperature persists even after the partition is unmounted (until I restart). As expected, I have run `btrfs check`, `btrfs balance`, `btrfs scrub` and `smartctl -t long /dev/nvme0` on both the subvolume partitions, neither of which show any sign of errors. From smartctl it can be seen, that the temperature keeps rising while no reads nor writes are performed (no r/w commands are being sent nor blocks are read). Do you please have some suggestions, what can I try? The obvious solution is to try to format the drive, but I want to explore related debugging rabbit holes first. Thanks!
